title: Classes
definition: TypeScript adds powerful static typing, access modifiers, and type-checking capabilities to standard ES6 JavaScript Classes.
simpleExplanation: A Class in JavaScript is a factory for creating objects. TypeScript turns that factory into a high-security facility. It ensures every worker (property) is accounted for, makes sure people can't enter restricted areas (private properties), and ensures the final product exactly matches the blueprint.
realWorldExample: Building an API service layer: `class UserService { fetchUser() { ... } }`.

basic: Do you need to declare class properties before using them in the constructor in TS?

answers.question: Do you need to declare properties first?
answers.answer: Yes! In vanilla JS, you can just do `this.name = name` in the constructor. In TS, you MUST declare `name: string;` at the top of the class body before using it in the constructor (unless using shorthand).

answers.question: What is strictPropertyInitialization?
answers.answer: If this flag is true, TS throws an error if you declare a class property (like `name: string;`) but forget to actually assign it a value inside the `constructor()`. It prevents undefined bugs.
